DEFINITION · qeva:1:random-variable@1

Random variable

A random variable converts outcomes into measurable values.

editorialprobability · statistics
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

A random variable converts outcomes into measurable values.

EXACT

The compact statement

A random variable X:(Ω,𝓕)→(S,Σ) is a measurable function: X⁻¹(A)∈𝓕 for every A∈Σ.

Example

For two coin tosses, X can count the number of heads.

Boundary / caveat

The variable is a function; randomness belongs to the probability model on outcomes.

Assumptions

  • The declared measure-theoretic probability context is fixed.
